content.raw_text: 哈利与德思礼一家相处的最后一个月并不愉快。说真的，达力着实被哈利吓坏了，他不敢跟哈利待在同一个房间里，佩妮姨妈和弗农姨父也不敢再把哈利关在碗柜里，也不强迫他干活儿了，也不再朝他大喊大叫—— 事实上，他们根本不跟他讲话。一半出于恐惧，一半由于恼怒，他们对哈利的存在视而不见。尽管这在许多方面是一个进步，但时间一久就使人感到有些没趣。

sentences.text: 哈利与德思礼一家相处的最后一个月并不愉快。
sentences.translation: Harry's last month with the Dursleys was not pleasant.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object, which is different from English. The negative form in Chinese is formed by adding '不' before the adjective.

sentences.text: 说真的，达力着实被哈利吓坏了，他不敢跟哈利待在同一个房间里，佩妮姨妈和弗农姨父也不敢再把哈利关在碗柜里，也不强迫他干活儿了，也不再朝他大喊大叫—
sentences.translation: Honestly, Dudley was really scared by Harry. He didn't dare to stay in the same room with Harry. Aunt Petunia and Uncle Vernon also didn't dare to lock Harry in the cupboard anymore, didn't force him to do chores, and didn't yell at him anymore—
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes how Dudley was scared of Harry to the point where he didn't want to be in the same room with him, and even Aunt Petunia and Uncle Vernon stopped mistreating Harry.
The sentence consists of a dash (em dash) used for separation or interruption.

sentences.text: 事实上，他们根本不跟他讲话。
sentences.translation: In fact, they don't talk to him at all.
sentences.explanation: The structure '根本不' together means 'not at all'. This sentence structure is commonly used in Chinese to emphasize the negation of an action.

sentences.text: 一半出于恐惧，一半由于恼怒，他们对哈利的存在视而不见。
sentences.translation: Half out of fear, half out of anger, they turned a blind eye to Harry's existence.
sentences.explanation: The structure '一半...一半...' is used to express 'half...half...'. The phrase '对...视而不见' means 'turn a blind eye to' in this context.

sentences.text: 尽管这在许多方面是一个进步，但时间一久就使人感到有些没趣。
sentences.translation: Although this is progress in many ways, over time it becomes somewhat boring.
sentences.explanation: The structure '尽管...但...' is a common way to express contrast in Chinese. The word '一久' means 'over time' or 'as time goes by'.

content.raw_text: 哈利大多时间都待在他的房间里，有他新买的猫头鹰做伴。他决定管它叫海德薇，这是他从<魔法史>这本书里找到的名字。他的学校课本都很有趣。他躺在床上，一读就到深夜，海德薇从打开的窗口尽情地飞进飞出。幸运的是佩妮姨妈不再到房间里来吸尘了，因为海德薇总是叼死耗子回来。哈利把九月一日以前每天的日期一天一天写在一张纸上，钉在墙上，每天临睡前就在第二天的日期上打一个钩。

sentences.text: 哈利大多时间都待在他的房间里，有他新买的猫头鹰做伴。
sentences.translation: Harry spends most of his time in his room, accompanied by his newly bought owl.
sentences.explanation: The structure '有...做伴' is a common way to express being accompanied by someone or something in Chinese.

sentences.text: 他决定管它叫海德薇，这是他从<魔法史>这本书里找到的名字。
sentences.translation: He decided to call it Hydevee, which is a name he found in the book <History of Magic>.
sentences.explanation: The structure '他决定管它叫' means 'He decided to call it'. The phrase '从...里找到' means 'found in'.

sentences.text: 他的学校课本都很有趣。
sentences.translation: His school textbooks are all very interesting.
sentences.explanation: The structure '都很' is used to emphasize that all of his school textbooks are very interesting.

sentences.text: 他躺在床上，一读就到深夜，海德薇从打开的窗口尽情地飞进飞出。
sentences.translation: He lay on the bed, reading until late at night, while Hedwig flew in and out through the open window.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes a scene where the character is lying on the bed reading until late at night, while Hedwig freely flies in and out through the open window. Pay attention to the use of the possessive particle '的' and the structure '一...就...' to indicate doing something immediately after another action.

sentences.text: 幸运的是佩妮姨妈不再到房间里来吸尘了，因为海德薇总是叼死耗子回来。
sentences.translation: Fortunately, Aunt Penny no longer comes to the room to vacuum, because Heidi always brings back dead mice.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes a situation where Aunt Penny no longer comes to vacuum the room because Heidi always brings back dead mice, implying that Aunt Penny is no longer needed for that task.

sentences.text: 哈利把九月一日以前每天的日期一天一天写在一张纸上，钉墙上，每天临睡前就在第二天的日期上打一个钩。
sentences.translation: Harry wrote the dates of each day before September 1st one by one on a piece of paper, nailed it to the wall, and put a check mark on the date of the next day before going to bed every night.
sentences.explanation: This sentence demonstrates the use of time-related vocabulary, possessive particles, and the structure of indicating the object of a verb using '把'.

words.definition: used to indicate the object of a verb

content.raw_text: 八月的最后一天，哈利觉得最好还是跟姨父姨妈谈谈明天去国王十字车站的事，于是他下楼来到起居室，姨父姨妈正在看竞猜电视节目。他清了一下嗓子，好让他们知道他来了；达力尖叫着跑出屋去。

sentences.text: 八月的最后一天，哈利觉得最好还是跟姨父姨妈谈谈明天去国王十字车站的事，于是他下楼来到起居室，姨父姨妈正在看竞猜电视节目。
sentences.translation: On the last day of August, Harry felt it was best to talk to his aunt and uncle about going to King's Cross Station tomorrow, so he went downstairs to the living room, where his aunt and uncle were watching a quiz TV show.
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces the setting and characters in the story. It shows Harry's decision to discuss his trip to King's Cross Station with his aunt and uncle, highlighting the family dynamics and everyday activities.

sentences.text: 他清了一下嗓子，好让他们知道他来了；
sentences.translation: He cleared his throat, so they would know he had arrived;
sentences.explanation: The structure '好让他们知道' means 'so that they would know'. The use of '了' indicates the completion of the action of clearing the throat.

sentences.text: 达力尖叫着跑出屋去。
sentences.translation: Dali ran out of the house screaming.
sentences.explanation: The structure '着' after a verb indicates that the action is in progress. In this sentence, it shows that Dali is screaming while running out of the house.

content.raw_text: “哦—— 弗农姨父?”弗农姨父哼了一声，表示他在听。

sentences.translation: Oh—
sentences.explanation: The character '哦' is an interjection used to express surprise or realization. The dash '—' is used for emphasis or to indicate a pause in speech.
The sentence consists of a dash/em dash, which is often used to indicate a break in thought or to separate clauses in Chinese writing.

sentences.text: 弗农姨父？
sentences.translation: Uncle Vernon?
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a question asking about Uncle Vernon, who is the father's sister's husband.

sentences.text: ”弗农姨父哼了一声，表示他在听。
sentences.translation: Uncle Vernon grunted, indicating that he was listening.
sentences.explanation: The structure '表示...在...' is used to indicate that someone is doing something, in this case, indicating that Uncle Vernon is listening.

content.raw_text: “哦—— 我明天得去国王十字车站—— 去霍格沃茨。” 弗农姨父又哼了一声。“请问您用车送我一下行吗?”“哼。”哈利认为这就是表示可以。“谢谢您。”他刚要回到搂上去，弗农姨父却真的开口说话了。

sentences.translation: Oh—
sentences.explanation: The character '哦' is an interjection used to express surprise, realization, or other emotions. The dash '—' here is used for emphasis or to indicate a pause in speech.
The sentence consists of a dash (em dash) which is used to indicate a break in thought or to set off parenthetical statements.

sentences.text: 我明天得去国王十字车站—
sentences.translation: I have to go to King's Cross Station tomorrow—
sentences.explanation: The structure '得去' indicates necessity or obligation in this sentence. The phrase '国王十字车站' refers to 'King's Cross Station' in English.
The em dash (——) is commonly used in Chinese writing to indicate a break or interruption in thought, similar to how it is used in English.

words.definition: em dash (used for emphasis or interruption)

sentences.text: 去霍格沃茨。
sentences.translation: Go to Hogwarts.
sentences.explanation: This sentence is a simple command telling someone to go to Hogwarts. 霍格沃茨 (Hogwarts) is the name of the famous wizarding school in the Harry Potter series.

sentences.text: ” 弗农姨父又哼了一声。
sentences.translation: Uncle Vernon snorted again.
sentences.explanation: The sentence uses the word "弗农" to refer to Uncle Vernon, which is a common way to address uncles in Chinese. The verb "哼" means to snort or make a snorting sound.

sentences.text: “请问您用车送我一下行吗？
sentences.translation: Can you give me a ride?
sentences.explanation: The structure '请问...吗?' is a polite way to ask a question in Chinese. The use of '您' is a polite form of 'you'. '用车' specifically means 'give a ride' in this context.

sentences.translation: Hmph.
sentences.explanation: This sentence consists of a sound interjection 'Hmph' followed by a period. The quotation marks at the beginning and end are used to indicate the speech tone.

sentences.text: ”哈利认为这就是表示可以。
sentences.translation: Harry thought this was a sign of approval.
sentences.explanation: The structure '这就是表示可以' can be translated as 'this was a sign of approval'. The word '可以' here means 'approval' in this context.

sentences.text: “谢谢您。
sentences.translation: Thank you.
sentences.explanation: The phrase '谢谢您' is a polite way to say 'thank you' in Chinese, with '您' being a formal form of 'you'.

sentences.text: ”他刚要回到搂上去，弗农姨父却真的开口说话了。
sentences.translation: He was just about to hug her, but Uncle Vernon really spoke up.
sentences.explanation: The structure 刚要...却真的...了 indicates an interruption or unexpected event happening right when something else was about to happen.

content.raw_text: “坐火车去巫师学校未免太可笑了。他们的魔毯全都破光了吗?”哈利没吭声。“这所学校到底在什么地方?你说。”“我不知道。”哈利说，刚刚才想到这一点。他从衣袋里掏出海格给他的火车票。叶“我应该坐十一点钟从934 站台开出的火车。” 他读道。他姨父姨妈瞪大了眼睛。“第几站台?”“9 43 站台。”

sentences.text: “坐火车去巫师学校未免太可笑了。
sentences.translation: Taking a train to the wizarding school is too ridiculous.
sentences.explanation: The structure '未免太' is used to express that something is excessively or overly a certain way.

words.definition: indicates completion or change of situation

sentences.text: 他们的魔毯全都破光了吗？
sentences.translation: Have all their magic carpets been completely worn out?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Possessive Particle + Object + Adverb + Verb + Particle indicating completion + Question Particle. The use of '吗' at the end turns the statement into a question.

sentences.text: ”哈利没吭声。
sentences.translation: Harry didn't say a word.
sentences.explanation: The structure 没 + verb is used to indicate the negation of an action in Chinese.

sentences.text: “这所学校到底在什么地方？
sentences.translation: Where exactly is this school located?
sentences.explanation: The phrase '到底' is used for emphasis to express 'exactly' or 'in the end'.

words.definition: measure word for buildings or institutions

sentences.text: 你说。
sentences.translation: You said.
sentences.explanation: This sentence consists of the subject '你' meaning 'you' and the verb '说' meaning 'said'. The period '。' indicates the end of the sentence.

sentences.text: ”“我不知道。
sentences.translation: I don't know.
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a simple statement expressing lack of knowledge. The word order in Chinese is Subject + 不 + Verb, which is different from English.

sentences.text: ”哈利说，刚刚才想到这一点。
sentences.translation: Harry said, just thought of this point.
sentences.explanation: The structure '刚刚才' is used to emphasize that the action just happened, similar to 'just' in English.

sentences.text: 他从衣袋里掏出海格给他的火车票。
sentences.translation: He took out the train ticket Hagrid gave him from his pocket.
sentences.explanation: The structure '从...里' is used to indicate where something is taken from. The possessive particle '的' is used to show possession.

sentences.text: 叶“我应该坐十一点钟从934 站台开出的火车。
sentences.translation: Ye: "I should take the train departing from platform 934 at eleven o'clock."
sentences.explanation: The structure '应该坐' means 'should take' in this context. The measure word '点' is used to indicate time in Chinese.

sentences.text: ” 他读道。
sentences.translation: He read.
sentences.explanation: The character '道' is a particle used after a verb to indicate the completion of an action. In this context, it signifies that the action of reading has been completed.

words.definition: particle indicating completion of an action

sentences.text: 他姨父姨妈瞪大了眼睛。
sentences.translation: His uncle and aunt widened their eyes.
sentences.explanation: In Chinese, family relationships are specified with precision. Here, 姨父 refers to the uncle who is the husband of the mother's sister, and 姨妈 refers to the aunt who is the mother's sister.

sentences.text: “第几站台？
sentences.translation: Which platform?
sentences.explanation: The sentence is asking about the specific platform number.

sentences.translation: 9 43 platform.
sentences.explanation: The sentence simply mentions the numbers 9 and 43 followed by the word 'platform'.
The sentence is incomplete and only contains a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “别胡说八道了，”弗农姨父说，“根本没有943 站台。”

sentences.text: “别胡说八道了，”弗农姨父说，“根本没有943 站台。
sentences.translation: Stop talking nonsense," Uncle Vernon said, "There is no Platform 943.
sentences.explanation: The sentence includes a common structure in Chinese where the verb '说' (said) comes after the subject and before the quote. The phrase '胡说八道' is an idiomatic expression meaning 'talking nonsense'.

words.definition: indicating completion or change of state

sentences.translation: The journey starting from platform 943.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object. In this sentence, '从' means 'from', '943' is a number, '站台' means 'platform', '开始' means 'start', and '的' is a possessive particle indicating 's.

content.raw_text: “我的火车票上就是这么写的。”

sentences.text: “我的火车票上就是这么写的。
sentences.translation: My train ticket is written like this.
sentences.explanation: The structure '就是这么' is a common way to express 'is exactly like this' in Chinese.

words.definition: particle indicating past tense or possession

sentences.explanation: The sentence ends with a quotation mark and an ellipsis, indicating a continuation or omission of text.

content.raw_text: “胡说，”弗农姨父说，“他们好多人都疯了，到处乱咋唿。你会明白的。你等着瞧吧。好了，我们送你去国王十字车站。反正我们明天要去伦敦，要不然我才不去找麻烦呢。”

sentences.text: “胡说，”弗农姨父说，他们好多人都疯了，到处乱咋唿。
sentences.translation: Nonsense,
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a colloquial expression '胡说' which means 'nonsense'. The structure '好多人都' means 'many of them have' in this context.

sentences.text: 你会明白的。
sentences.translation: You will understand.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + 会 + Verb + 的. The particle 的 is used to indicate possession or completion in this context.

sentences.text: 你等着瞧吧。
sentences.translation: Just you wait and see.
sentences.explanation: The structure '等着 + verb' is used to indicate waiting for something to happen. The modal particle '吧' is often used to soften a suggestion or emphasize a statement.

words.definition: modal particle indicating suggestion or emphasis

sentences.text: 好了，我们送你去国王十字车站。
sentences.translation: Okay, we will take you to King's Cross Station.
sentences.explanation: The structure '送你去' means 'take you to' in this context. '国王十字车站' refers to 'King's Cross Station'.

sentences.text: 反正我们明天要去伦敦，要不然我才不去找麻烦呢。
sentences.translation: Anyway, we are going to London tomorrow, otherwise I wouldn't bother.
sentences.explanation: The structure '要不然' is used to express 'otherwise'. The use of '才' in this context indicates a hypothetical situation where the speaker wouldn't bother doing something.

sentences.translation: The journey starting from platform 943.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object, so the word order may seem different from English. In this sentence, the journey is the subject, starting from platform 943 is the verb-object phrase, and 的 is a possessive particle indicating ownership.

content.raw_text: “您上伦敦做什么?”哈利问，希望保持友好气氛。

sentences.text: “您上伦敦做什么？
sentences.translation: What are you doing in London?
sentences.explanation: The structure '您上...做什么?' is a common way to ask someone what they are doing in a specific place.

sentences.text: ”哈利问，希望保持友好气氛。
sentences.translation: Harry asked, hoping to maintain a friendly atmosphere.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Verb + Object. The tricky part for learners might be the use of the word '希望' (hope) followed by '保持' (maintain), which together convey the idea of 'hoping to maintain' in English.

content.raw_text: “带达力上医院，”弗农姨父咆哮起来，“在他上斯梅廷之前把那条可恶的尾巴割掉。”

sentences.text: “带达力上医院，”弗农姨父咆哮起来，在他上斯梅廷之前把那条可恶的尾巴割掉。
sentences.translation: Take Dali to the hospital," Uncle Vernon roared, "cut off that wretched tail before he goes to Smelting.
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains imperative form (带), directional complement (上), and the structure '在...之前' meaning 'before'. The phrase '把...割掉' indicates cutting off something.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 第二天，哈利早上五点就醒来了。他又兴奋又紧张，再也睡不着了。他从床上爬起来，穿上牛仔裤，因为他不愿穿巫师长袍进火车站—— 他准备上车再换。他又核对了一遍霍格沃茨开列的购物单，看需要的东西是否都买齐了，再看看海德薇是不是好好地关在笼子里，之后就在房间里踱起步来，等候德思礼夫妇起床。两小时后，哈利沉重的大箱子终于被抬上了德思礼家的汽车，佩妮姨妈说服达力坐到哈利身边，他们就上路了。

sentences.text: 第二天，哈利早上五点就醒来了。
sentences.translation: The next day, Harry woke up at five in the morning.
sentences.explanation: The structure '就...了' is used to indicate that an action happens earlier or more quickly than expected.

words.definition: indicating that the action happens earlier than expected

sentences.text: 他又兴奋又紧张，再也睡不着了。
sentences.translation: He was excited and nervous, unable to sleep anymore.
sentences.explanation: The structure '又...又...' is used to express two different emotions or states that occur simultaneously. The word '了' at the end of the sentence indicates a change in the situation, emphasizing that he can no longer sleep.

sentences.text: 他从床上爬起来，穿上牛仔裤，因为他不愿穿巫师长袍进火车站—
sentences.translation: He got up from the bed, put on jeans, because he didn't want to wear a wizard robe to the train station—
sentences.explanation: The sentence showcases the use of verbs '爬起来' (climb up) and '穿上' (put on), as well as the structure '因为' (because) to indicate the reason for an action.
The em dash (—) is a punctuation mark used to indicate a break in thought or to set off parenthetical statements. In this context, it is likely used to introduce a new section or emphasize a point.

words.definition: em dash (used for emphasis or interruption)

sentences.text: 他准备上车再换。
sentences.translation: He is ready to get on the train and transfer again.
sentences.explanation: The structure '上车再换' means 'get on the train and transfer again.' The verb '上车' means 'get on the train' and '再' indicates doing the action again.

sentences.text: 他又核对了一遍霍格沃茨开列的购物单，看需要的东西是否都买齐了，再看看海德薇是不是好好地关在笼子里，之后就在房间里踱起步来，等候德思礼夫妇起床。
sentences.translation: He checked the shopping list prepared by Hogwarts again, to see if everything needed was bought, then checked if Hedwig was safely locked in the cage, and then paced around the room, waiting for the Dursleys to wake up.
sentences.explanation: The sentence involves checking items on a list, ensuring a pet is secure, and waiting for someone to wake up.

sentences.text: 两小时后，哈利沉重的大箱子终于被抬上了德思礼家的汽车，佩妮姨妈说服达力坐到哈利身边，他们就上路了。
sentences.translation: Two hours later, Harry's heavy trunk was finally lifted onto the Dursleys' car, Aunt Petunia persuaded Dudley to sit next to Harry, and they set off.
sentences.explanation: This sentence contains a possessive structure '哈利的大箱子' (Harry's big trunk) and a persuasive structure '佩妮姨妈说服达力坐到哈利身边' (Aunt Petunia persuaded Dudley to sit next to Harry).

content.raw_text: 他们十点半钟来到国王十字车站。弗农姨父把哈利的皮箱放到手椎车上．帮他推进站。哈利正在琢磨弗农姨父为什么一下子变得出奇地好，弗农姨父突然面对站台停下来不走了，心怀鬼胎地咧嘴一笑。

sentences.text: 他们十点半钟来到国王十字车站。
sentences.translation: They arrived at King's Cross Station at half past ten.
sentences.explanation: The structure '十点半' means 'half past ten', and '国王十字车站' refers to 'King's Cross Station'.

sentences.text: 弗农姨父把哈利的皮箱放到手椎车上．帮他推进站。
sentences.translation: Uncle Vernon put Harry's trunk on the trolley and helped him push it into the station.
sentences.explanation: The structure '把...放到...' is a common way to express putting something on something else in Chinese.

sentences.text: 哈利正在琢磨弗农姨父为什么一下子变得出奇地好，弗农姨父突然面对站台停下来不走了，心怀鬼胎地咧嘴一笑。
sentences.translation: Harry was wondering why Uncle Vernon suddenly became unusually nice. Uncle Vernon suddenly stopped in front of the platform, smirked with a sinister smile.
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains some idiomatic expressions like "出奇地" (unusually) and "心怀鬼胎" (smirked with a sinister smile), which may be challenging for intermediate learners.

content.raw_text: “好了，你到了，小子。第9站台—— 第10站台。你的站台应该是在这两个站台之间吧，可看起来好像还没来得及修建呢，是吧?”

content.raw_text: 他拦住一个过路的警卫，但不敢提943 站台。警卫从来没听说过霍格沃茨。当他发现哈利甚至说不清霍格沃茨具体在什么地方时，他开始生气了，认为哈利故意装傻愚弄他。哈利实在没辙了，只好问十一点发出的列车有几班。警卫说一班也没有。最后警卫迈着大步走开了，一路抱怨有些人专门浪费别人的时间。这时哈利告诫自己尽量不要惊慌失措。到达列车时刻表上方的大钟显示，再过十分钟他就该登上开往霍格沃茨的列车了，可他一点也不知道该怎么办。他身边是一只他简直提不动的大箱子，满满一口袋魔币和一只大猫头鹰，他站在站台中央，一筹莫展。

sentences.text: 警卫说一班也没有。

sentences.text: 最后警卫迈着大步走开了，一路抱怨有些人专门浪费别人的时间。

sentences.text: 这时哈利告诫自己尽量不要惊慌失措。

sentences.text: 到达列车时刻表上方的大钟显示，再过十分钟他就该登上开往霍格沃茨的列车了，可他一点也不知道该怎么办。
sentences.translation: The clock above the train schedule shows that in ten minutes he should board the train to Hogwarts, but he has no idea what to do.

sentences.text: 他身边是一只他简直提不动的大箱子，满满一口袋魔币和一只大猫头鹰，他站在站台中央，一筹莫展。
sentences.translation: Next to him was a large suitcase that he could hardly lift, filled with a pocketful of wizard coins and a large owl, he stood in the middle of the platform, at his wits' end.

sentences.text: “我听说你后来跟麻瓜们住在一起。
sentences.translation: I heard you later lived with Muggles.
sentences.explanation: The structure '跟...一起' means 'together with'. '麻瓜' (Muggles) refers to non-magical people in the Harry Potter universe.

sentences.text: ”罗恩说，“他们怎么样？
sentences.translation: Ron said, "How are they?"
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is a simple question asking about the well-being of a group of people. The use of quotation marks indicates direct speech.

sentences.text: ”“太差劲了，当然不是所有的人都这样。
sentences.translation: It's too bad, of course not everyone is like that.
sentences.explanation: The structure '不是...都这样' is a common way to say 'not everyone is like that' in Chinese.

sentences.text: 不过我的姨父姨妈和表哥都太差劲了。
sentences.translation: But my uncle, aunt, and cousin are all too lousy.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Possessive Particle + Family Members + 都 + Adjective + 了.

sentences.text: 我要是有三个巫师兄弟就好了。
sentences.translation: I wish I had three wizard brothers.
sentences.explanation: The structure '要是' is used to express a wish or desire in Chinese.

sentences.translation: The journey starting from platform 943.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object. In this sentence, the subject is implied (the journey), followed by the verb 'start' and the object 'platform 943'. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate that the platform belongs to the journey.

content.raw_text: “五个。”罗恩说，不知为什么他显得有些不高兴。“我是我们家去霍格沃茨上学的第六个了。你可以说，我应当以他们为榜样。比尔和查理已经毕业了。比尔是男生学生会主席，查理是魁地奇球队队长。现在珀西当上了级长，弗雷德和乔治尽管调皮捣蛋，但他们的成绩是顶哌哌的。大家都觉得他们很有意思，都盼望我能跟他们一样。话说回来，如果我能做到，也没什么了不起的了，因为他们在我之前就做到了。你要是有五个哥哥，你就永远用不上新东西。我穿比尔的旧长袍，用查理的旧魔杖，还有珀西扔了不要的老鼠。”

sentences.text: “五个。
sentences.translation: Five.
sentences.explanation: The sentence simply means 'five' in English. The measure word '个' is used here to indicate a general count of five.

sentences.text: ”罗恩说，不知为什么他显得有些不高兴。
sentences.translation: Ron said, for some reason he seemed a bit unhappy.
sentences.explanation: The structure '不知为什么' is a common way to express 'for some reason' in Chinese.

sentences.text: “我是我们家去霍格沃茨上学的第六个了。
sentences.translation: I am the sixth one in our family to go to Hogwarts for school.
sentences.explanation: The structure '第...个了' is used to indicate the ordinal number of something in a sequence.

words.definition: particle indicating completion or change of situation

sentences.text: 你可以说，我应当以他们为榜样。
sentences.translation: You can say, I should take them as role models.
sentences.explanation: The structure '以...为...' means 'take...as...' in this context.

sentences.text: 比尔和查理已经毕业了。
sentences.translation: Bill and Charlie have already graduated.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure follows the subject-verb-object pattern commonly used in Chinese. The use of '了' at the end of the sentence indicates that the action of graduating has been completed.

sentences.text: 比尔是男生学生会主席，查理是魁地奇球队队长。
sentences.translation: Bill is the male student council president, Charlie is the Quidditch team captain.
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces two characters and their respective roles. '男生' specifically means 'male student' in this context, and '魁地奇' refers to the fictional sport Quidditch from the Harry Potter series.

sentences.text: 现在珀西当上了级长，弗雷德和乔治尽管调皮捣蛋，但他们的成绩是顶哌哌的。
sentences.translation: Now Percy has become a prefect, although Fred and George are mischievous, their grades are excellent.
sentences.explanation: The sentence showcases the structure '虽然...但是...' (although...but...), which is commonly used to express contrast in Chinese.

sentences.text: 大家都觉得他们很有意思，都盼望我能跟他们一样。
sentences.translation: Everyone thinks they are very interesting, and they all hope I can be like them.
sentences.explanation: The structure '都...都' emphasizes that everyone has the same feeling or hope. The word '能' indicates ability or possibility.

sentences.text: 话说回来，如果我能做到，也没什么了不起的了，因为他们在我之前就做到了。
sentences.translation: Speaking of which, if I can do it, it's nothing special, because they did it before me.
sentences.explanation: The structure '如果...，也没什么了不起的了' is a common way to express that achieving something is not a big deal, especially when others have done it before.

sentences.text: 你要是有五个哥哥，你就永远用不上新东西。
sentences.translation: If you have five older brothers, you will never need new things.
sentences.explanation: This sentence illustrates a conditional statement using '要是' (if). It also shows the use of '就' (then) to indicate a consequence.

sentences.text: 我穿比尔的旧长袍，用查理的旧魔杖，还有珀西扔了不要的老鼠。
sentences.translation: I wear Bill's old robe, use Charlie's old wand, and Percy threw away an old mouse.
sentences.explanation: The structure '还有' is used to connect items in a list, similar to 'and' in English.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

sentences.text: 罗恩说着，伸手从上衣内袋里掏出一只肥肥的灰老鼠，它正在睡觉。
sentences.translation: Ron said, reaching into the inner pocket of his jacket, he pulled out a chubby gray old mouse that was sleeping.
sentences.explanation: This sentence contains a complex structure where the action of reaching into the pocket and pulling out the mouse is described before the subject 'Ron' is mentioned. This might be confusing for learners as the subject is not introduced immediately.

sentences.text: “它叫斑斑，已经毫无用处了，整天睡不醒。
sentences.translation: It's called Banban, already useless, sleeping all day without waking up.
sentences.explanation: The structure '已经毫无用处了' means 'already useless'. The repetition of '斑斑' emphasizes the name. The phrase '整天睡不醒' means 'sleeping all day without waking up'.

sentences.text: 珀西当上了级长，我爸送给他一只猫头鹰，他们买不起—

sentences.translation: Ron's ears turned red.

sentences.text: 他似乎觉得自己话太多，就又开始看着窗外。
sentences.translation: He seemed to think he talked too much, so he started looking out the window again.

sentences.translation: This seems to have improved Ron's mood a lot.

sentences.translation: Saying his name, it's not because I'm brave or anything.
sentences.explanation: The structure '并不是因为' means 'it's not because' in this context. The possessive particle '的' is used after nouns to indicate possession.

sentences.text: ”哈利说。

sentences.text: 我相信，我有许多东西需要学。
sentences.translation: I believe, I have many things to learn.
sentences.explanation: The structure '需要 + verb' is used to express 'need to do something'.

sentences.translation: He said again, it can be heard that he has been feeling anxious about this recently, "I dare say, I will definitely be the worst student in the class."
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is different from English, with the verb often placed before the subject. The phrase '正为此感到忧心忡忡' uses the structure '正 + verb' to indicate an ongoing action. The phrase '我敢说' means 'I dare say', where '敢' means 'dare' and '说' means 'say'.

sentences.text: ，“不会的。

sentences.explanation: The structure "不会的" means "don't know" in this context, with the possessive particle 的 indicating the negation of knowing something.

sentences.text: 有很多学生都来自麻瓜家庭，可他们也学得很快。
sentences.translation: Many students come from Muggle families, but they also learn very quickly.
sentences.explanation: The structure '虽然...可是...' (although...but...) is commonly used in Chinese to express contrast.

sentences.text: ” 在他们谈话的时候，列车已驶出伦敦。
sentences.translation: While they were talking, the train had already left London.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在...的时候' is used to indicate an action happening at the same time as another action. The word '已' is used to indicate that the action has already taken place.

sentences.text: 这时他们正沿着遍地牛羊的田野飞驰。
sentences.translation: At this time, they were galloping along fields full of cattle and sheep.
sentences.explanation: The structure '正...飞驰' indicates an action in progress, similar to 'were galloping' in English.

sentences.translation: They fell silent for a moment, watching the fields and grasslands pass by.

sentences.translation: When he was at the Desli family, he never spent a penny to buy candy to eat. Now his pockets are filled with jingling gold coins and silver coins.

sentences.text: 随之而来的是一片树林，弯弯曲曲的河流和暗绿色的山丘。
sentences.translation: Following that is a forest, winding rivers, and dark green hills.
sentences.explanation: The structure '随之而来的' is a formal way to indicate 'following that'. The measure word '一片' is used for land or areas.

sentences.text: 又有人敲他们的隔闻门。
sentences.translation: Someone knocked on their compartment door again.
sentences.explanation: The structure '有人' is used to mean 'someone'. The word '隔闻' specifically refers to a compartment in this context.

sentences.text: 与哈利在934 站台擦肩而过的圆脸男孩走进来，满眼含泪。
sentences.translation: The round-faced boy who passed by Harry at platform 934 walked in, eyes brimming with tears.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes a round-faced boy who passed by Harry at platform 934, walking in with tears in his eyes.

sentences.text: “对不起，”他说，“我想问问，你看见我的蟾蜍了吗？
sentences.translation: I'm sorry,
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is a common pattern in Chinese where the speaker apologizes before asking a question. The use of 了 at the end of the sentence indicates that the action of seeing the toad is completed.

sentences.text: ” 哈利和罗恩都摇摇头，他就大哭起来。
sentences.translation: Harry and Ron both shook their heads, and he started crying.
sentences.explanation: The structure '就...起来' is used to indicate that an action begins or intensifies. In this sentence, it shows that the person started crying.

sentences.text: “我又把它弄丢了！
sentences.translation: I lost it again!
sentences.explanation: The structure '把 + object + verb + 了' is a common way to express the completion of an action in Chinese.

words.definition: indicating the object of the verb

sentences.text: 它总想从我身边跑掉！
sentences.translation: It always wants to run away from me!
sentences.explanation: The structure '总想' means 'always wants' in this context. '身边' means 'side' or 'beside'.

sentences.text: ”“它会回来的。
sentences.translation: It will come back.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + 会 + Verb + 的. The use of 的 at the end indicates possession or completion of an action.

sentences.text: ”哈利说。
sentences.translation: Harry said.
sentences.explanation: The sentence consists of the character 哈利 (Harry) followed by the verb 说 (said), indicating that Harry is the speaker in this context.

content.raw_text: “是啊，”孩子伤心地说，“那么，要是你们看见..”

sentences.text: “是啊，”孩子伤心地说，那么，要是你们看见。
sentences.translation: Yes,
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Adverb + Verb, which is different from English. The use of quotation marks '“”' indicates direct speech.
The sentence contains opening and closing quotation marks, indicating a direct quotation or specific reference.

content.raw_text: 他走了。

sentences.text: 他走了。
sentences.translation: He left.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is subject + verb + particle '了' to indicate completion of the action.

content.raw_text: “我不明白，他为什么这么着急。”罗恩说，“我要是买了一只蟾蜍，我会想办法尽快把它弄丢，越快越好。不过我既然带了斑斑，也就没话可说了。”

sentences.text: “我不明白，他为什么这么着急。
sentences.translation: I don't understand why he is in such a hurry.
sentences.explanation: The structure '为什么' means 'why' in this context. The combination '这么' means 'such' in this sentence.

sentences.text: ”罗恩说，“我要是买了一只蟾蜍，我会想办法尽快把它弄丢，越快越好。
sentences.translation: Ron said, 'If I bought a toad, I would find a way to lose it as soon as possible, the sooner the better.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence showcases a conditional structure '要是' (if), the use of measure word '只' for small animals, and the comparison structure '越...越...' (the more... the more...).

words.definition: measure word for small animals like frogs/toads
particle marking the following noun as the object of the verb

sentences.text: 不过我既然带了斑斑，也就没话可说。
sentences.translation: But since I brought Banban, I have nothing to say.
sentences.explanation: The structure '既然...也就...' indicates a causal relationship, meaning 'since...then...'. The use of '了' after a verb indicates the completion of the action.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 老鼠还在罗恩的腿上打盹。

sentences.text: 老鼠还在罗恩的腿上打盹。
sentences.translation: The mouse is napping on Ron's leg.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在...上' is used to indicate the location of an action or state, in this case, the mouse napping on Ron's leg.

content.raw_text: “它说不定早死了，反正死活都一样。”罗恩厌烦地说，“我昨天试着想把它变成黄色的，变得好玩一些，可是我的咒语不灵。我现在来做给你看看，注意了..”

sentences.text: “它说不定早死了，反正死活都一样。
sentences.translation: It might have died long ago, anyway, dead or alive, it's all the same.
sentences.explanation: The structure '不定...反正...都一样' is a common way to express indifference or that the outcome doesn't matter.

sentences.text: ”罗恩厌烦地说，“我昨天试着想把它变成黄色的，变得好玩一些，可是我的咒语不灵。
sentences.translation: Ron said irritably, 'I tried to turn it yellow yesterday to make it more fun, but my spell didn't work.'
sentences.explanation: This sentence includes the structure '试着 + verb' to indicate trying to do something. The use of '的' after '咒语' indicates possession, making it 'my spell'.

sentences.text: 我现在来做给你看看，注意了。
sentences.translation: I will do it for you to see, pay attention.
sentences.explanation: The structure '来做给你看看' means 'to do it for you to see', which is a common way to express showing or demonstrating something to someone in Chinese.
This sentence only consists of a period, indicating the end of a thought or sentence.
This sentence only contains a closing quotation mark and a space.

content.raw_text: 他在皮箱里摸索了半天，拽出一根很破旧的魔杖，有些地方都剥落了，一头还闪着白色亮光。

sentences.text: 他在皮箱里摸索了半天，拽出一根很破旧的魔杖，有些地方都剥落了，一头还闪着白色亮光。
sentences.translation: He rummaged in the trunk for a long time, pulling out a very old wand, some parts of which were peeling off, with one end still shining white light.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes the action of a person rummaging in a trunk and finding an old wand with some parts peeling off but still emitting white light from one end.

content.raw_text: “独角兽毛都要露出来了。不过..”

sentences.text: “独角兽毛都要露出来了。
sentences.translation: The unicorn's fur is about to be exposed.
sentences.explanation: The sentence uses the structure '都...了' to indicate that something is about to happen or has already happened. In this case, it emphasizes that the unicorn's fur is almost completely exposed.

sentences.text: 不过。
sentences.translation: However.
sentences.explanation: The word 不过 is used to introduce a contrasting or unexpected statement.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 他刚举起魔杖，隔间门又开了。那个丢蟾蜍的男孩再次来到他们俩面前，只是这回有一个小姑娘陪他同来。她已经换上了霍格沃茨的新长袍。

sentences.text: 他刚举起魔杖，隔间门又开了。
sentences.translation: He just raised his wand, and the compartment door opened again.
sentences.explanation: The structure 刚...又...了 is used to indicate that an action happened again in quick succession. In this sentence, 刚 indicates that the action of raising the wand was just completed, and 又...了 indicates that the door opened again immediately after.

sentences.text: 那个丢蟾蜍的男孩再次来到他们俩面前，只是这回有一个小姑娘陪他同来。
sentences.translation: The boy who lost the toad came in front of them again, but this time with a little girl accompanying him.
sentences.explanation: The sentence showcases the structure of '只是...，这回...' meaning 'but this time'. It also introduces the verb '陪' meaning 'to accompany'.

sentences.text: 她已经换上了霍格沃茨的新长袍。
sentences.translation: She has already changed into the new robe of Hogwarts.
sentences.explanation: The structure '已经 + Verb + 了' is used to indicate that an action has already been completed. The possessive particle '的' is used to show possession or association between '霍格沃茨' (Hogwarts) and '新长袍' (new robe).

content.raw_text: “你们有人看到一只蟾蜍吗?纳威丢了一只蟾蜍。”她说，语气显得自高自① 由豆加咸肉、糖浆、番茄酱制成。

sentences.text: “你们有人看到一只蟾蜍吗？
sentences.translation: Have any of you seen a toad?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is a typical Chinese question format with the question particle '吗' at the end. The word '一只' is a measure word used for small animals like toads.

sentences.text: 纳威丢了一只蟾蜍。
sentences.translation: Nawei lost a toad.
sentences.explanation: The sentence follows the subject-verb-object structure commonly used in Chinese sentences. The word '了' indicates a change of state, suggesting that the action of losing the toad has been completed.

sentences.text: ”她说，语气显得自高自① 由豆加咸肉，糖浆，番茄酱制成。
sentences.translation: She said, in a tone that seemed arrogant, made from soybeans, salted pork, syrup, and ketchup.
sentences.explanation: The structure '自...自...' is used to indicate an excessive or arrogant manner. In this context, it describes the tone of the speech.

content.raw_text: 大，日中无人。她有一头浓密的棕色头发和一对大门牙。

sentences.text: 大，日中无人。
sentences.translation: Big, no one in the middle of the day.
sentences.explanation: The structure '日中' means 'in the middle of the day' in this context. It's a common way to express time in Chinese.

sentences.text: 她有一头浓密的棕色头发和一对大门牙。
sentences.translation: She has thick brown hair and a pair of big front teeth.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the structure of '有' (to have) in Chinese, where the possession is indicated before the possessed item. Additionally, '一对' is used to express 'a pair of' in Chinese.

content.raw_text: “我们已经对他说过了，我们没有看见。”罗恩说，可小姑娘根本不理会，只看着他手里的魔杖。

sentences.text: “我们已经对他说过了，我们没有看见。
sentences.translation: We have already told him that we did not see.
sentences.explanation: The structure '对...说' means 'tell (someone)' in Chinese. The particle '了' indicates the completion of the action.

sentences.text: ”罗恩说，可小姑娘根本不理会，只看着他手里的魔杖。
sentences.translation: Ron said, but the little girl completely ignored him, only looking at the wand in his hand.
sentences.explanation: The structure '可...根本不...' is a common way to express 'but completely not' in Chinese.

content.raw_text: “哦。你是在旋魔法吗?那就让我们开开眼吧。”

sentences.translation: Oh.
sentences.explanation: The word '哦' is used to express a light exclamation or realization. It is commonly used in informal conversations.

sentences.text: 你是在旋魔法吗？
sentences.translation: Are you using magic?
sentences.explanation: The structure '是在' is used to ask if someone is currently doing something. '吗' is a question particle used at the end of a sentence to indicate a yes-no question.

sentences.text: 那就让我们开开眼吧。
sentences.translation: Let's open our eyes.
sentences.explanation: The structure '让...开...' means 'let's open...' and '吧' is used to make a suggestion in a softer tone.
The sentence contains a quotation mark and an ellipsis, indicating that there is more text following this sentence.

content.raw_text: 她坐了下来。罗恩显然吃了一惊，有些不知所措。

sentences.text: 她坐了下来。
sentences.translation: She sat down.
sentences.explanation: The structure 坐了下来 indicates the completion of the action of sitting down.

sentences.text: 罗恩显然吃了一惊，有些不知所措。
sentences.translation: Ron was obviously taken aback and somewhat at a loss.
sentences.explanation: The structure '有些不知所措' means 'somewhat at a loss' or 'not knowing what to do'.

sentences.translation: Oh—
sentences.explanation: The interjection '哦' is used to express surprise, realization, or other emotions. The dash '—' is used for a pause or interruption in speech.
The em dash (—) is used in Chinese text to indicate a break or interruption in the sentence.

words.definition: em dash (indicating a break or interruption)

sentences.text: 好吧。
sentences.translation: Okay.
sentences.explanation: The word '吧' at the end of the sentence is used to soften the tone or suggest something, making the sentence sound more polite or less assertive.

words.definition: indicating suggestion or softening of tone

sentences.explanation: The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 他清了清嗓子。

sentences.text: 他清了清嗓子。
sentences.translation: He cleared his throat.
sentences.explanation: The structure '清了清' is a duplication of the verb 'clear' to emphasize the action of clearing the throat.

content.raw_text: 雏菊、甜奶油和阳光，把这只傻乎乎的肥老鼠变黄。

sentences.text: 雏菊，甜奶油和阳光，把这只傻乎乎的肥老鼠变黄。
sentences.translation: Daisies, sweet cream, and sunshine turn this silly fat old mouse yellow.
sentences.explanation: The sentence uses the structure '把...变' to indicate the change of color happening to the mouse due to the daisies, sweet cream, and sunshine.

content.raw_text: 他挥动魔杖，但什么也没有发生。斑斑还是灰色的，睡得正香。

sentences.text: 他挥动魔杖，但什么也没有发生。
sentences.translation: He waved the wand, but nothing happened.
sentences.explanation: The structure '但什么也没有' means 'but nothing happened', where '也' is used to emphasize 'nothing'.

sentences.text: 斑斑还是灰色的，睡得正香。
sentences.translation: Spotted or gray, sleeping soundly.
sentences.explanation: The structure '睡得 + adj.' is a common way to describe how someone is doing an action.

content.raw_text: “你肯定这真是一道咒语吗?”小姑娘问。“看来不怎么样，是吧?我在家里试过几道简单的咒语，只是为了练习，而且都起作用了。我家没有一个人懂魔法，所以当我收到入学通知书时，我吃惊极了，但又特别高兴，因为，我的意思是说，据我所知，这是一所最优秀的魔法学校—— 所有的课本我都背会了，当然，我只希望这能够用—— 我叫赫敏格兰杰，顺便问一句，你们叫什么名字?”

sentences.text: “你肯定这真是一道咒语吗？
sentences.translation: Are you sure this is a real spell?
sentences.explanation: The structure '这真是一道' is a common way to express 'this is a real...' in Chinese.

sentences.text: ”小姑娘问。
sentences.translation: The little girl asked.
sentences.explanation: The sentence consists of the words 'little', 'girl', 'ask', and a period. The tricky part may be understanding the use of '小' to indicate 'little' before 'girl'.

sentences.text: “看来不怎么样，是吧？
sentences.translation: It doesn't seem so, right?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is a simple question formed by combining '看来' (it seems) with '不怎么样' (not so) and ending with '吧' (right?).

sentences.text: 我在家里试过几道简单的咒语，只是为了练习，而且都起作用了。
sentences.translation: I have tried several simple spells at home just for practice, and they all worked.
sentences.explanation: The structure '只是...而且...' is used to express 'just...and...' in this sentence.

sentences.text: 我家没有一个人懂魔法，所以当我收到入学通知书时我吃惊极了，但又特别高兴，因为，我的意思是说，据我所知，这是一所最优秀的魔法学校—
sentences.translation: My family doesn't have anyone who understands magic, so when I received the acceptance letter, I was extremely surprised, but also very happy, because, I mean, as far as I know, this is one of the best magic schools—
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces the speaker's surprise and happiness upon receiving an acceptance letter to a magic school, highlighting the lack of magical knowledge in their family.
The sentence consists of an em dash, which is used to indicate a break or pause in writing. In this context, it serves as a separator or divider in the text.

sentences.text: 所有的课本我都背会了，当然，我只希望这能够用—
sentences.translation: I have memorized all the textbooks, of course, I just hope this can be used—
sentences.explanation: The structure '希望这能够用' means 'hope this can be used', where '这' refers to the action or situation mentioned before.
The sentence consists of an em dash, which is a punctuation mark used to indicate a pause or break in a sentence.

sentences.text: 我叫赫敏格兰杰，顺便问一句，你们叫什么名字？
sentences.translation: My name is Hermione Granger, by the way, what are your names?
sentences.explanation: The structure '顺便问一句' is a common way to say 'by the way' before asking a question in Chinese.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 她连珠炮似的一气说完。

sentences.text: 她连珠炮似的一气说完。
sentences.translation: She finished speaking in one breath like a string of firecrackers.
sentences.explanation: The phrase '连珠炮' is used metaphorically to describe speaking quickly and continuously, like the rapid succession of firecrackers going off.

content.raw_text: “我叫罗恩韦斯莱。”罗恩嘟哝说。

sentences.text: “我叫罗恩韦斯莱。
sentences.translation: My name is Ron Weasley.
sentences.explanation: The structure '我叫' is used to introduce oneself by saying 'I am called'.

sentences.text: ”罗恩嘟哝说。
sentences.translation: Ron muttered.
sentences.explanation: This sentence is a simple statement where Ron is muttering.

content.raw_text: “哈利波特。”哈利说。

sentences.text: “哈利波特。
sentences.translation: Harry Potter.
sentences.explanation: This sentence simply consists of the name 'Harry Potter' in Chinese.

sentences.text: ”哈利说。
sentences.translation: Harry said.
sentences.explanation: This sentence consists of the character for Harry's name followed by the verb 'said', ending with a period. The quotation mark at the beginning indicates speech.

content.raw_text: “真的是你吗?”赫敏问。“你的事我全都知道。当然—— 我额外多买了几本参考书，《现代魔法史》、《黑魔法的兴衰》、《二十世纪重要魔法事件》，这几本书里都提到了你。”

sentences.text: “真的是你吗？
sentences.translation: Is it really you?
sentences.explanation: The structure '真的是你吗?' is a common way to ask if something is really someone or something.

sentences.text: ”赫敏问。
sentences.translation: Hermione asked.
sentences.explanation: This sentence is a simple question where Hermione is asking something. The structure is straightforward and does not contain any complex grammar points.

sentences.text: “你的事我全都知道。
sentences.translation: I know everything about your matters.
sentences.explanation: The structure '全都' together means 'all' in this context, emphasizing the speaker knows everything.

sentences.text: 当然—
sentences.translation: Of course—
sentences.explanation: The em dash at the end of the sentence indicates a pause or interruption in speech.
The em dash is used in Chinese text to indicate a break or interruption in the narrative.

words.definition: em dash (indicating a break or interruption)

sentences.text: 我额外多买了几本参考书，《现代魔法史》，《黑魔法的兴衰》，《二十世纪重要魔法事件》，这几本书里都提到了你。
sentences.translation: I bought several extra reference books, 'Modern History of Magic', 'The Rise and Fall of Dark Magic', 'Important Magical Events of the Twentieth Century', all of which mention you.
sentences.explanation: The sentence showcases the use of enumeration markers '、' to list multiple items and the particle '了' to indicate the completion of an action.

sentences.explanation: The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “提到我?”哈利说，突然感到一阵头晕目眩。

sentences.text: “提到我？
sentences.translation: Mention me?
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a simple question asking if the speaker is being mentioned.

sentences.text: ”哈利说，突然感到一阵头晕目眩。
sentences.translation: Harry said, suddenly feeling a wave of dizziness.
sentences.explanation: The structure '突然感到' means 'suddenly feeling' in this context. The phrase '一阵' is used to quantify the feeling of dizziness.

content.raw_text: “天哪，你居然会不知道。要是我，我一定想办法把所有提到我的书都找来。”赫敏说，“你们俩知不知道自己会被分到哪个学院?我已经到处打听过了，我希望能分到格兰芬多，都说那是最好的，我听说，邓布利多自己就是从那里毕业的，不过我想拉文克劳也不算太坏..不管怎么说，我们最好还是先去找纳威的蟾赊。你们俩最好赶快把衣服换上，要知道，我们大概很快就要到了。”

sentences.text: “天哪，你居然会不知道。
sentences.translation: Oh my, you actually don't know.
sentences.explanation: The structure '居然' is used to express surprise or disbelief, similar to 'actually' in English.

sentences.text: 要是我，我一定想办法把所有提到我的书都找来。
sentences.translation: If it were me, I would definitely find all the books that mention me.
sentences.explanation: The structure '把...找来' indicates the action of finding something.

words.definition: particle used to shift the object to before the verb

sentences.text: ”赫敏说，“你们俩知不知道自己会被分到哪个学院？
sentences.translation: Hermione said, 'Do you two know which house you'll be sorted into?'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is a question embedded in a statement, asking if the two people know which house they will be sorted into.

sentences.text: 我已经到处打听过了，我希望能分到格兰芬多，都说那是最好的，我听说，邓布利多自己就是从那里毕业的，不过我想拉文克劳也不算太坏。
sentences.translation: I have inquired everywhere, hoping to be sorted into Gryffindor. They all say it's the best. I heard that Dumbledore himself graduated from there. But I think Ravenclaw isn't too bad either.
sentences.explanation: The sentence expresses the speaker's desire to be sorted into Gryffindor, which is considered the best house. It also mentions Dumbledore graduating from Gryffindor, but the speaker thinks Ravenclaw is also a decent option.

sentences.text: 不管怎么说，我们最好还是先去找纳威的蟾赊。
sentences.translation: Anyway, we'd better go find Nawei's toad first.
sentences.explanation: The structure '不管...还是' is used to express 'anyway' or 'regardless of'. The word '最好' means 'had better' and '先' indicates doing something first.

sentences.text: 你们俩最好赶快把衣服换上，要知道，我们大概很快就要到了。
sentences.translation: You two had better change your clothes quickly, you know, we will probably arrive soon.
sentences.explanation: The structure '把...换上' is a common way to express 'change into' in Chinese.

words.definition: indicating a thing is affected by an action

sentences.explanation: The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 于是她领着那个丢蟾蜍的男孩一道走了。

sentences.text: 于是她领着那个丢蟾蜍的男孩一道走了。
sentences.translation: So she led the boy who lost the toad away.
sentences.explanation: The structure '一道' here means 'together' or 'along with'. It is commonly used in Chinese to indicate doing something together with someone else.

sentences.translation: Someone tried to rob the highly guarded underground vault.

content.raw_text: “什么事也没有，正因为这样才爆出一件大新闻。他们没有被抓住。我爸爸说，显然只有功力最高强的黑巫师才能设法摆脱古灵阁的追捕。不过他们什么也没有拿走，怪就怪在这里。当然，每当这类事情发生时，就人人自危，人们担心事情背后有神秘人指使。”
